messages:
Marta: Heads-up: noticed persistent AZ imbalance when scale-to-zero runs in eu-west1. One zone (eu-west1-b) keeps losing GPU nodes from preemptions and kube-scheduler ends up moving pods -> request retries.

Kevin: Seen it. Spot preempts in b, autoscaler then spins up nodes in other AZs. Pods with zone affinity suffer cold starts and some model servers fail healthchecks.

Ashok: Tried a small "hibernate window" prototype. Instead of immediate node termination we annotate the node `hibernating=true` and keep local model KV cache warm for 15m. If a request arrives we remove the annotation and skip the heavy model reload. Cuts cold-starts ~2.5x in staging.

Marta: Nice. How did you hook it? Cluster-Autoscaler change or separate controller?

Ashok: Lightweight controller + autoscaler integration. Autoscaler still decides the node is unneeded but posts an event; our controller marks it hibernating and delays the final drain/terminate for the window. Quick sketch of the config (informal):

```yaml
# prototype controller config (informal)
autoscaler:
  scaleDownUnneededTime: 10m
  scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 20m

controller:
  hibernateWindow: 15m
  preemptibleBias: 0.6  # prefer to keep non-preemptible in primary AZ
```

Ryan: What's the cost tradeoff? 15m idle GPUs = extra $ for idle capacity.

Ashok: In staging we saw ~5% hourly GPU spend increase for eu-west1 fleets, but 40% fewer request retries and p99 latency improved significantly. For our hosted customers that saw retries, net ROI was positive due to fewer replays and support tickets.

Sophie: We should pair this with topologySpreadConstraints / preferredDuringScheduling to avoid tight AZ packing. Also consider explicit pool mixes: non-preemptible in primary AZ, spot in secondary AZ, so hibernate helps recover without forcing cross-AZ migrations.

Kevin: Agreed. Also tune CA flags to reduce thrash: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`, `--scale-down-delay-after-add=20m`, `--max-node-provision-time=10m`. The controller needs to annotate so CA doesn't prematurely consider the node fully removed.

Kevin: Note: CA doesn't know our custom `hibernating` lifecycle; we rely on the controller to finish the node termination after the window or when marked safe.

infra-ops-bot: Warning: last night eu-west1-b had 12 preemptions in a 40m window. See: https://internal.metrics/redwood/eu-west1/preemptions (chart).

Marta: Action items: 1) small staging experiment with controller + 15m hibernateWindow (@Kevin to PR), 2) cost sims with 3 pool mixes (@Sophie), 3) chaos tests for AZ preemption and node flapping (@Ryan).

Kevin: Will open PR today for a proof-of-concept controller and autoscaler hook.

Sophie: I'll run cost sims and push numbers by EOD.

Ryan: I'll add chaos experiments (preempt nodes in a single AZ) to the staging pipeline and report results.

deploy-bot: rollout/gpu-hibernate-controller v0.1 deployed to staging :rocket:

Marta: Thanks team. If staging looks good we can do a 24h canary in eu-west1 with ~20% of GPU capacity on the controller to validate customer impact. :thumbsup:
